chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Kansas City, silent movie organ and drumming for Chauncey Downs
summary: He lived in Kansas City, Kansas for a year while his mother played in theatres, and he once played drums with Chauncey Downs's band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So I lived in Kansas City, Kansas. She was playing --

you know, during those times they had the silent movies, and they would have the organist to play during the movie, showing of the movie. My mother did this, she went to Kansas City and she worked. There was one theatre, I forget this theatre, but it was at 18th and Vine or someplace.

Yeah, yeah. She played for a theatre there, and she also played for another theatre in Kansas City, Kansas. So I went to school in Kansas City, Kansas, and I was looking through a book the other day and I saw a name, Chauncey Downs. And I remember that my mother played with him at Excelsor Springs, Missouri, and they didn't have a drummer and I played drums and I had never played drums before in my life. But I played drums with Chauncey's band, and I had the opportunity to see him -- I only lived there for a little over a year, then we went back south. But I saw Chauncey once after that. He was living in Lansing, Michigan, and I was there with Roy Eldridge. And someone happened to mention his name and I went to see him and it was -- he remembered me, as the drummer.
No, never played drums since my legs were -- it was very tiring, you know. I never played drums after that.
